thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Extend Gains as Trump Unveils Budget, Infrastructure Plan

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Extend Gains as Trump Unveils Budget, Infrastructure Plan
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Monday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +1.5%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +1.8%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +1.6%
PowerShares QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +1.8%
iProShares Trust Ultra VIX Short Term Futures ETF ( UVXY ): -4.6%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were firmer. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 1.8%.
US stocks continued to trade in positive territory at session's half, with the energy sector emerging as the forerunner among gainers after prices for crude oil rebounded from a selloff last week.
The US benchmarks were pursuing a recovery after sharp losses last week saw the S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nasdaq Composite all down more than 5% over the five days. In Monday's session, the Dow was led by gains in Apple (AAPL) and Cisco Systems (CSCO).
Wall Street has turned its focus on President Donald Trump's newly unveiled $4 trillion budget, including a pay raise for troops and billions to build a southern border wall and spending related to the opioid crisis. The adminsitration will also be rolling out an infrastructure plan to spend $200 billion over the next 10 years for infrastructure grants to states and cities.
For the rest of the week, investors will be watching closely data on consumer and production inflation, retail sales, and consumer sentiment.
Power Play: Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 2.0% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 1.9%.
Houston American Energy (HUSA) shares rose 18.0% after the Permian Basin-focused exploration and production company said preliminary data for Q4 pegs revenue at $414,743, up 842% from a year ago and 271% sequentially. Production volume estimates totaled 6,150 barrels of oil and 19,518 thousand cubic feet of gas (or 9,403 barrels of oil equivalent) compared with 1,395 boe of production a year earlier and 2,885 boe sequentially. Realized prices for oil and gas were $54.05/Bbl and $4.22/Mcf compared to $44.94/Bbl and $2.93/Mcf for Q4 2016 and $43.45/Bbl and $3.29/Mcf for Q3 2017.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 1.8%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 3.8% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 4.0%.
Deutsche Bank AG (DB) was up 3.3% after it said it has agreed to repay more than $3.7 million to customers in relation to an investigation by the US Securities and Exchange Commission that found that traders and salespeople made false and misleading statements while negotiating sales of commercial mortgage-backed securities.
Technology
Tech funds Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK), iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were weaker. Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 1.0% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 1.1%.
CoreLogic (CLGX) rose 1.1% said it has completed its acquisition of eTech Solutions Limited, a UK-based provider of innovative mobile surveying and workflow management software. With more than 50% of UK property appraisals running through the eTech platform in 2017, the company provides an end-to-end property valuation workflow management platform and mobile appraiser solution. eTech clients include UK appraisers, appraisal management companies and lenders.
Commodities
Crude was down 3.2%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 0.8%. Natural gas was down 4.1% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.7%.
Gold was down 0.1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.7%. Silver was down 0.9%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 1.8%.
Health Care
Health care funds Health Care SPDR (XLV), Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH), were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 1.8%
Dare Bioscience (DARE) rose more than 47% after it said that it has entered into an agreement to license SST-6007, a potential treatment for female sexual arousal disorder, from Strategic Science & Technologies, LLC. SST-6007 incorporates sildenafil, the same active ingredient in Viagra, in a proprietary cream formulation. If approved, Dare believes SST-6007 would be the first FDA-approved treatment for FSAD.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP), Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were weaker.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in the red.
Iconix Brand Group (ICON) surged 35% after the company announced it has reached agreements with holders of approximately $110 million principal amount of its 1.5% convertible notes due March 2018 to exchange their notes for new senior subordinated convertible notes and cash payments representing accrued but unpaid interest. The company also announced a cost savings initiative to improve its profitability and free cash flow. The company said it expects to achieve annual savings of approximately $12 million through proactive rightsizing of its expense structure, appropriately aligned to its expected go-forward revenue base.
